extracted.intended_audience: students and researchers pursuing academic careers in mathematics (undergraduates, graduate students, postdocs, and early-career mathematicians)
extracted.subtask_description: A broad collection of practical career and professional-development advice for people at various stages of a mathematics career (primary school through postdoc/early-career faculty), focused on academic trajectories, research practice, and time management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice on gifted education (primary school)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice on gifted education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link/reference to resources about educating gifted primary-school students; no expanded guidance on-page beyond providing the topic/link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice on mathematics competitions (high school)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice on mathematics competitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pointer to materials about competing in mathematical contests for high-school students; the page lists this as a topic of advice without full exposition here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing which universities to apply to
rubrics_metrics.description: What universities should one apply to?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A topical pointer implying thoughtful selection of institutions; elsewhere the page cautions against basing decisions on glamour or fame and recommends studying at different places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Become better at solving mathematical problems (undergraduate)
rubrics_metrics.description: How can one become better at solving mathematical problems?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes the central idea that mathematical development is not only about grades/exams or formal methods but also about problem-solving practice; points to further resources (links) on problem-solving techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematics is more than grades, exams, rigour, and proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: More to maths than grades and exams and methods; more to maths than rigour and proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages valuing creativity, intuition, informal thinking, and partial results rather than focusing solely on formal correctness or high marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value partial progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Value partial progress as a crucial stepping stone to a complete solution of a problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat intermediate or partial results as important and legitimate progress; use them as building blocks for further advances rather than dismissing them as 'not the full solution.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't base career decisions on glamour or fame
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't base career decisions on glamour or fame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice to avoid choosing institutions, topics, or paths solely for prestige; instead weigh other factors (fit, mentorship, training opportunities). This admonition is paired with the recommendation to study at different places.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study at different places
rubrics_metrics.description: Study at different places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourages exposure to varied institutions and environments to broaden training, perspectives, and networks; implied as a complement to avoiding glamour-based choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work hard and work professionally (graduate level)
rubrics_metrics.description: It is important to work hard, and work professionally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General guidance that sustaining effort and professional conduct are essential in graduate training; suggests maintaining high standards of reliability, communication, and research discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enjoy your work
rubrics_metrics.description: But it is also important to enjoy your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation to cultivate intrinsic interest and satisfaction in research to sustain long-term productivity and well-being; balancing effort with enjoyment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think ahead to understand the way forward
rubrics_metrics.description: Think ahead to understand the way forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan research directions and milestones so you have a sense of trajectory; envision next steps to avoid aimless wandering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask yourself dumb questions to understand the way before
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask yourself dumb questions to understand the way before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use basic, naive, or 'obvious' questions to clarify understanding, expose hidden assumptions, and reveal tractable subproblems; this is a technique to get unstuck and to demystify a problem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attend talks and conferences beyond your immediate area
rubrics_metrics.description: Attend talks and conferences, even those not directly related to your own work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broaden exposure to different techniques and ideas, which can spawn new problems and collaborations; recommended even if content doesn't immediately match your projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talk to your advisor but also take the initiative
rubrics_metrics.description: Talk to your advisor, but also take the initiative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use your advisor as a primary resource because they know your situation, but proactively direct your research, propose projects, and seek other mentors when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't prematurely obsess on a single 'big problem' or 'big theory'
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't prematurely obsess on a single “big problem” or “big theory”.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid tunnel vision early in a career; explore a range of problems and methods to build skills and avoid wasting time on hopeless projects before you have adequate tools or background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write down what you've done and make your work available
rubrics_metrics.description: Write down what you’ve done, and make your work available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep written records of progress, drafts, and expositions; disseminate via preprints, talks, or publications. The page links to additional advice on how to write and submit papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn and relearn your field (postdoc)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn and relearn your field, but don't be afraid to learn things outside your field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continually refresh core knowledge while branching into adjacent or new areas to expand tools and perspectives; postdoc stage is for consolidating breadth as well as depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn limitations and power of tools; continually aim just beyond your range
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn the limitations of your tools, but also learn the power of other mathematician’s tools. In particular, you should continually aim just beyond your current range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand where your preferred techniques fail and where others succeed; choose problems that stretch you slightly beyond your comfort zone to foster growth without overreaching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be flexible and patient in research
rubrics_metrics.description: In your research, be both flexible and patient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt when approaches fail, be willing to change direction, and allow time for ideas to mature; avoid forcing quick outcomes at the expense of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and present research; be considerate of your audience
rubrics_metrics.description: You should definitely travel and present your research if given the opportunity. But be considerate of your audience; talks are not the same as papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seize opportunities to give talks for visibility and feedback, but tailor presentations to the audience (broader exposition, less technical detail) and recognize the different goals of talks vs. written papers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be sceptical of your own work and use the wastebasket
rubrics_metrics.description: Be sceptical of your own work, and don’t be afraid to use the wastebasket.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically evaluate your results; discard ideas or writeups that are unproductive or incorrect rather than clinging to them for sunk-cost reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time management: batch low-intensity tasks together
rubrics_metrics.description: Batch low-intensity tasks together to take advantage of economies of scale and to reduce distraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group routine, low-cognitive-load tasks into dedicated blocks (email, admin, small chores) to protect deep-work time and reduce context switching; part of a broader time-management strategy for researchers (links to more thoughts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult community resources and colleagues
rubrics_metrics.description: Use community resources and the broader academic community for career development (links to many external advice pages and blogs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page curates external guides (e.g., John Baez, Oded Goldreich, Richard Hamming, Matt Might, Ravi Vakil, etc.); consult these as complementary perspectives and practical guides for different career stages.
